sn22.55:1.3: I follow the interpretation established by Bhikkhu Bodhi, for which see his note 75 on this discourse in *Connected Discourses*. When using first person pronouns, the formula epitomizes the annihilationist view: “I might not be” ([sn22.81:11.9](), [sn24.4:1.3](), [sn22.153:1.3](), [an10.29:19.1]()). The Buddha reformed it with the impersonal third person pronoun: “It might not be”.
sn22.55:8.9: “Will vanish” is _vibhavissati_, literally “will cease to be”, the verbal form of the word “nonexistence” (_vibhava_) in the second noble truth. It’s used throughout [snp4.11]() and, in a meditation context, in [an11.9:7.1](). At [iti49:7.3]() it refers to the ending of continued existence for an arahant.
sn22.55:9.4: Here the monk quotes the Buddha, as indicated by the close _-ti_ in the text.
sn22.55:10.1: This question is also at [sn22.81:4.4](). “Without delay” means “in this very life”.
